mainTopic: בכורים: when they become holy, רב ששת's rule on הנחה and קריאה, and רבי ישמעאל's proof that מעשר שני depends on the בית המקדש
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rule about בכורים: a non-כהן is liable for eating them only once they enter the בית המקדש, which matches רבי אליעזר's view that בכורים outside are חולין and those inside are הקדש. Next, רב ששת rules that הנחה (placing the fruits by the מזבח) is essential for בכורים, but קריאה (reading the פסוקים) is not. The גמרא supports him from a ברייתא in which רבי ישמעאל asks whether מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים today. He tries comparisons to בכור and to בכורים, each is refuted, and he finally learns from a פסוק that links מעשר to בכור. Since the ברייתא attacked בכורים only for needing הנחה and never for קריאה, the גמרא says קריאה must not be essential. רב אשי rejects this proof: the תנא left out קריאה because a גר brings בכורים without reading, so קריאה does not apply in every case. The גמרא then explains why a מה הצד argument could not replace the פסוק, and asks what רבי ישמעאל holds about the lasting holiness of ירושלים. רבינא answers with a בכור whose meat is compared to its blood. The amud closes by explaining that the double הקש is allowed because מעשר דגן is חולין.

steps.title: Liability for eating first fruits starts when they enter the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The liability for eating בכורים begins only once the fruits reach the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when is a person liable for eating בכורים? From the moment they 'see the face of the House,' meaning they enter the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a rule from just before this point. Someone who is not a כהן becomes liable for eating בכורים only after the fruits have entered the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכורים are not fully holy from the moment they are picked or set aside. Their strict holiness, with its punishment for a non-כהן who eats them, begins only once they arrive at the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits, brought to the בית המקדש and given to the כהן
From when?
Liable for punishment
Literally 'the face of the House'; here, inside the בית המקדש

phrases.english: From when is one liable for them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the בכורים from the line just before. Some versions leave out the מ in round brackets.

phrases.english: From when they will see the face of the House.
phrases.notes: He means: once the fruits are brought inside the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement about בכורים that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for a non-כהן eating בכורים begins only once they enter the בית המקדש.

steps.title: This rule follows רבי אליעזר: outside is ordinary, inside is holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies רבי אליעזר as the source: בכורים outside the מקדש are treated like חולין, and those inside like הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It follows this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, if some בכורים are outside and some are inside, the ones outside are like ordinary produce in every way, and the ones inside are like holy property in every way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the rule from step 1. It answers with רבי אליעזר, who says location decides the status of בכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats bunches of the same fruit differently based only on where they are. Fruits outside are fully חולין and fruits inside are fully הקדש. That is exactly why liability starts only at entry into the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Which תנא holds this?)
A sage of the משנה period
Ordinary, non-holy produce
Consecrated, holy property
In every respect

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with this tanna,
as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
First fruits, some of which are outside
and some of which are inside,
phrases.notes: Outside or inside the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: those that are outside are like non-sacred produce
for all matters concerning them;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבִּפְנִים – הֲרֵי הֵן כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: those that are inside are like consecrated property for all matters concerning them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the תנא behind the rule in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that liability for בכורים begins once they enter the בית המקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אליעזר: בכורים outside are חולין, inside are הקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: For בכורים, according to רבי אליעזר, location decides holiness: outside means חולין, inside means הקדש.

steps.title: Placing first fruits is essential; reading the verses is not
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that הנחה is essential for בכורים, while קריאה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת says: for בכורים, placing them by the מזבח is essential, but reading the פסוקים is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule begins. רב ששת separates two parts of the בכורים ceremony: one is essential, and leaving out the other does not ruin the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing בכורים includes placing the basket by the מזבח (הנחה) and reading the פסוקים of 'ארמי אובד אבי' (קריאה). Without הנחה the מצוה is not done properly. Without קריאה it still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing the בכורים before the מזבח
Reading the פסוקים said when bringing בכורים
Holds back, is essential; without it the מצוה is not valid

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says: First fruits —
placement is essential for them;
recitation is not essential for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule about בכורים, not tied to the previous discussion of liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For בכורים, הנחה is essential and קריאה is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard for what is truly needed to fulfill the מצוה of בכורים.

steps.title: Source for רב ששת: רבי ישמעאל asks about second tithe today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds a תנא who agrees with רב ששת: a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל asks whether מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים without the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It follows this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says three things in the name of three elders. רבי ישמעאל says: I might think a person may bring מעשר שני up to ירושלים nowadays and eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a long ברייתא to show where רב ששת's rule comes from. Right now it only sets up רבי ישמעאל's question; the link to רב ששת comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether מעשר שני, which must be eaten in ירושלים, still applies after the חורבן. The connection to בכורים is not visible yet. It appears only at the end, when בכורים are used in the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Three elders; earlier sages whose teachings רבי יוסי passed on
'I might have thought'; opens a possibility the ברייתא will examine
Second tithe, eaten by the owner in ירושלים
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רב ששת's rule in these opening lines. The ברייתא is about מעשר שני. The link to רב ששת only becomes clear in Step 10, where the גמרא points out that the ברייתא attacked בכורים for needing הנחה but never for needing קריאה.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with this tanna, as it is taught:
Rabbi Yosei says three statements
in the name of three elders,
Rabbi Yishmael says:
One might think a person may bring second tithe up
in the present time to Jerusalem, and eat it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן – כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the search for a תנא who supports רב ששת.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's rule that הנחה is essential for בכורים but קריאה is not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל (through רבי יוסי) about eating מעשר שני nowadays.

steps.title: Proposed proof: second tithe is like a firstborn animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל suggests a comparison: בכור and מעשר שני both must be brought to ירושלים, and a בכור works only when the מקדש stands, so מעשר שני should be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical: a בכור must be brought to 'the place,' and מעשר שני must be brought to 'the place.' Just as a בכור applies only when the בית המקדש stands, so too מעשר שני applies only when the בית המקדש stands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל offers a logical argument for why מעשר שני should not be eaten nowadays. He compares it to a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both share one feature: each must be brought to ירושלים. Since a בכור is clearly tied to the בית המקדש, he suggests מעשר שני is too. This is a proposal that will be tested next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is logical'; introduces a reasoned argument
Firstborn kosher animal, brought as a קרבן
Requires
Bringing to 'the place,' meaning ירושלים

phrases.english: And it is a logical inference:
A firstborn requires bringing to the place,
and second tithe requires bringing to the place;

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת –
phrases.english: just as a firstborn is only in the presence of the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: so too, tithe is only in the presence of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a logical answer to the question raised in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר שני cannot be eaten without the בית המקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparison to בכור: both require הבאת מקום, and בכור applies only when the מקדש stands.

steps.title: Objection: a firstborn also needs its blood placed on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fails, because a בכור needs blood and parts offered on the מזבח, which explains why it depends on the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a בכור? It is special because it needs its blood and fats placed on the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא attacks its own comparison. A בכור is different from מעשר שני in an important way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור depends on the מקדש because it needs a working מזבח for its blood and אימורין. מעשר שני only has to be eaten in ירושלים, so the reason a בכור needs the מקדש may not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about X? It is special because...'; a standard way of breaking a comparison
Placing the blood on the מזבח
The fat parts of a קרבן burned on the מזבח
The altar

phrases.english: What about a firstborn? It is notable in that it requires
placement of blood and sacrificial portions upon the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the בכור comparison from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between בכור and מעשר שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בכור has a unique feature, the מזבח service, that explains why it needs the מקדש, and מעשר שני lacks that feature.

steps.title: Answer: first fruits prove the altar is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: בכורים have no blood on the מזבח, yet they too apply only when the מקדש stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא defends its comparison by bringing in בכורים. They have no blood service, yet they are still tied to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בכורים depend on the מקדש without any מתן דמים, the blood service cannot be the real reason. So the shared feature, bringing to ירושלים, should be enough to make מעשר שני depend on the מקדש too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove'; brings a case that shows the objection's feature does not matter

phrases.english: First fruits will prove it.
phrases.notes: בכורים need no blood on the מזבח, yet they are brought only when the מקדש stands.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example showing the objection's distinguishing feature is not decisive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור's dependence on the מקדש comes from its blood service, so מעשר שני cannot be learned from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: בכורים depend on the מקדש without blood service, so blood service is not the reason.

steps.title: Objection: first fruits require placement by the altar
steps.stepSummary: The proof from בכורים is attacked: they need הנחה by the מזבח, which מעשר שני does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about בכורים? They are special because they need to be placed by the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now attacks the proof from בכורים. They also have a link to the מזבח: they must be placed before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בכורים need הנחה by the מזבח, they too can be explained as depending on the מקדש for that reason, and מעשר שני has no such step. Notice that only הנחה is mentioned as what makes בכורים special. This is where the link to רב ששת's rule from step 3 begins to show.

keyTerms.meaning: Require placement by the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא treats הנחה as the defining requirement of בכורים. That is the hook the גמרא uses to connect this ברייתא to רב ששת's rule that הנחה is essential.

phrases.english: What about first fruits? They are notable in that they require placement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from בכורים given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using בכורים as proof that מעשר שני depends on the מקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בכורים have their own link to the מזבח (הנחה) that explains their dependence on the מקדש, and מעשר שני lacks it.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל concludes from a פסוק that links מעשר to בכור
steps.stepSummary: After his own comparisons were knocked down, רבי ישמעאל proves from a פסוק that מעשר שני is linked to בכור. So מעשר applies only when the מקדש stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And you shall eat there before ה׳ your God, etc.' It compares מעשר to בכור. Just as בכור is only when the Temple stands, so too מעשר is only when the Temple stands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל stops relying on logic and brings a פסוק that places מעשר and בכור side by side. This finishes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logical comparisons in Steps 5-8 each failed because of a difference involving the מזבח. A הקש from the פסוק does not need the two cases to be logically alike, because the Torah itself joined them. So the rule of בכור carries over to מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. Used to introduce the real source after logic has failed.
Compares, through a הֶקֵּשׁ: the Torah links two things in one verse, so they share rules.
In the presence of the Temple, meaning while the בית המקדש stands.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's final source is a הקש from the פסוק: מעשר is like בכור, so both apply only when the מקדש stands.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And you shall eat [there] before the Lord your God, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 14:23, a verse that lists the tithe and the firstborn together. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: It compares tithe to firstborn:

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִפְנֵי הַבַּיִת –
phrases.english: just as a firstborn is only when the Temple stands,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִפְנֵי הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: so too, tithe is only when the Temple stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְאָכַלְתָּ שָּׁם לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical proofs from בכור and בכורים were refuted, the ברייתא settles the question with a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מעשר שני may be eaten in ירושלים only when the מקדש stands, learned through a הקש to בכור.

steps.title: How the ברייתא supports רב ששת: it never attacked בכורים for needing קריאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where the support for רב ששת is. The תנא attacked בכורים only for needing הנחה, not for needing קריאה, so קריאה must not be essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were so that קריאה is essential, the תנא should have refuted: what about בכורים? They need both קריאה and הנחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the proof for רב ששת from this ברייתא. The proof is based on what the תנא left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8 the תנא pushed back on the comparison to בכורים only because they need הנחה by the מזבח. If קריאה (reciting the פרשה) were essential to בכורים, that would have been an even stronger difference from מעשר שני. Since the תנא did not mention it, it seems קריאה does not hold back the מצוה, just as רב ששת says.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so; it opens a test of what would follow from a claim.
Let him refute, meaning he should have raised this difference to break the comparison.

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from what the תנא did NOT say. The point is the missing objection about קריאה, not anything the ברייתא states outright.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if קריאה really were essential to בכורים.

phrases.english: let him refute: what about first fruits?
They require recitation and placement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the ברייתא now quoted in full, the גמרא spells out how it supports רב ששת, as promised in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that קריאה does not hold back the מצוה of בכורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's attack on בכורים in Step 8, which mentions only הנחה and leaves out קריאה.

steps.title: רב אשי: even without עיכוב there is still a מצוה, so the תנא should have mentioned it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes back on the proof. Even if קריאה is not essential, everyone agrees it is a מצוה, so the תנא could have attacked with that. Leaving it out proves nothing about עיכוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Granted there is no requirement that holds it back, but is there no מצוה? Let the תנא say 'there is a מצוה' and refute with that!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues that the missing mention of קריאה cannot prove anything about whether it is essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even according to רב ששת, reciting the פרשה is still a מצוה with בכורים, and מעשר שני has no such מצוה. That difference alone would have been enough to break the comparison. So the תנא's silence must have some other reason, and it does not show that קריאה is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: An essential requirement; without it the act does not count.
Here: something one should do, even though skipping it does not ruin the act.
Granted that... An opening that concedes one point before making another.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Granted that there is no invalidation,
is there no מצוה?
So let him say 'מצוה' and refute!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: נְהִי דְּעִיכּוּבָא לֵיכָּא, מִצְוָה מִי לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof for רב ששת drawn in Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא, without ruling on רב ששת's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Silence about קריאה cannot show it is not essential, since even a plain מצוה would have been a good enough difference to mention.

steps.title: רב אשי's real reason for the silence: a גר cannot do קריאה, so it is not universal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new reason for the תנא's silence. A גר brings בכורים but cannot say 'that ה׳ swore to our fathers', so קריאה does not apply to every case of בכורים. A תנא only uses a difference that holds in all cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Since there are בכורים of a convert, who would need to say 'that ה׳ swore to our fathers' but cannot say it, קריאה is not a rule that holds in every case, so the תנא did not use it.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 11 showed that the תנא's silence about קריאה must have some other reason. Here רב אשי gives that reason, which finishes knocking down the proof for רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A refutation (פירכא) works best when the difference applies to all בכורים. Because a גר brings בכורים without reciting, קריאה is not a feature of every case. הנחה is, so the תנא used only הנחה. That explains the silence without saying anything about whether קריאה is essential.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought by a convert.
It is not clear-cut or across the board for him; it does not apply in every case.
Rather. It shows the earlier explanation is dropped and a new one is coming.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general Talmudic habit: a תנא prefers a difference that applies in every case (פסיקא) when he refutes a comparison.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Since there are the first fruits of a convert,
who would need to say
"that the Lord swore to our fathers,"
phrases.notes: דברים 26:3. ה׳ made this promise to the forefathers of the Jewish people, not to the convert's own ancestors, so he can't honestly say it.

phrases.english: and he cannot say it,
it is not clear-cut for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא בִּכּוּרֵי הַגֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason for the תנא's silence that Step 11 showed was still needed (since even a plain מצוה would have been worth mentioning).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof for רב ששת from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנא left out קריאה because it does not apply to every case (בכורי הגר), not because it is non-essential.

steps.title: Why not derive it with a מה הצד argument from בכור and בכורים together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק was needed. Each of בכור and בכורים was refuted on its own, but together they could support a מה הצד argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the reasoning go back to the start and derive it through 'what is the common factor'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the הקש. It suggests combining the two failed comparisons into one stronger argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכור was refuted because it has blood on the מזבח (Step 6), and בכורים because they need הנחה (Step 8). But בכורים have no blood and בכור has no הנחה, so each cancels the other's weak point. What remains in common is that both are brought to ירושלים and both apply only when the מקדש stands. Then מעשר שני should follow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the common side': a proof from two cases whose weak points cancel out, leaving a shared feature.
Let the reasoning go back, meaning return to the earlier logical comparisons.

phrases.english: And let the reasoning return to the start,
and derive it through 'what is the common factor'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא needed the הקש of Step 9 when logic could still work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the הקש from the פסוק in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Combining בכור and בכורים in a מה הצד cancels each one's weak point, so a פסוק should be unnecessary.

steps.title: The מה הצד fails: both cases have a connection to the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The מה הצד can be refuted. Both בכור and בכורים involve the מזבח in some way, and מעשר שני does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it can be refuted: what about the common factor of the two? They both have an aspect of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13 by showing that the combined argument also has a weak point, so the פסוק really was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases differ in how they connect to the מזבח (blood for בכור, הנחה for בכורים), but both do connect to it. מעשר שני has no connection to the מזבח at all. So the shared feature might be what ties them to the מקדש, and the proof cannot carry over to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The common factor shared by the two source cases.
Some connection to the altar.

steps.whatToRemember: A מה הצד argument breaks down if the two source cases share an extra feature that the new case lacks. Here that feature is a link to the מזבח.

phrases.english: Because it can be refuted:
what about the common factor in them?
They have an aspect of the altar.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a weak point that the מה הצד argument shares in both source cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Combining בכור and בכורים would prove the rule for מעשר שני without a פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources involve the מזבח and מעשר שני does not, so the הקש from the פסוק is needed.

steps.title: What does רבי ישמעאל hold about the lasting holiness of ירושלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what view רבי ישמעאל holds about קדושה ראשונה. Under either view, it seems בכור and מעשר שני should be in the same position, so why was בכור obvious to him while מעשר was a question?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does he hold? If he holds that the first holiness made the place holy for its time and also for the future, then בכור too should be brought now. If he holds it made the place holy for its time but not for the future, then even בכור should be a question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי ישמעאל's starting assumption. He treated בכור as obviously needing the מקדש while asking only about מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ירושלים kept its holiness after the חורבן, a בכור could still be brought and eaten there, so it would not depend on the מקדש. If the holiness ended, then בכור should be just as unclear as מעשר שני. Either way, the gap between בכור and מעשר in the ברייתא seems hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: The first holiness, given to ירושלים and the מקדש in the days of שלמה.
It made the place holy for its own time.
For the future, meaning even after the חורבן.
It should be asked, meaning it should be left as an open question.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about מעשר שני directly. It asks why רבי ישמעאל treated בכור as obvious in the first place.

phrases.english: And what does he hold?
If he holds that the first holiness
made it holy for its time and made it holy for the future,
then a firstborn too should apply,
phrases.notes: He means a בכור could also be brought and eaten in ירושלים today.

phrases.english: If he holds that the first holiness

phrases.aramaic: קִדְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְלֹא קִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא –
phrases.english: made it holy for its time but did not make it holy for the future,
then even a firstborn should be a question!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִדְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְקִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the basic assumption of the ברייתא from Step 5, that בכור clearly depends on the מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's assumption that בכור obviously depends on the מקדש while מעשר שני is in doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: under either view of קדושה ראשונה, בכור should be in the same position as מעשר שני.

steps.title: רבינא explains the firstborn case through a comparison of meat to blood
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says רבי ישמעאל holds קדשה לשעתה ולא קדשה לעתיד לבא. The בכור ruling is about a בכור whose blood was sprinkled before the חורבן. Its meat is compared to its blood, so it needs a standing מזבח. מעשר is then compared to בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, רבי ישמעאל holds that the first sanctification was only for its own time, not for the future. Here we are talking about a בכור whose blood was sprinkled before the בית המקדש was destroyed. Then the בית המקדש was destroyed while its meat was still around. We compare its meat to its blood: just as its blood needs the מזבח, so its meat needs the מזבח. And מעשר is compared to בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question from Step 15. He shows that the בכור ruling rests on its own special reason, a הקש of meat to blood, and is not only about the holiness of ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 asked why בכור and מעשר שני would ever be treated differently. רבינא narrows the בכור case to one where the blood was already sprinkled, so the only question is eating the meat. Since the פסוק links the meat to the blood, eating the meat also needs a standing מזבח. מעשר is tied to בכור by a second comparison, and that sets up the next objection.

keyTerms.meaning: The destruction of the בית המקדש.
A comparison the תורה makes by placing two things together, so the law of one applies to the other.
We compare one thing to another through a הקש.

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer moves the reason for the בכור ruling to a הקש. That opens the door to the next question about whether a law learned from a הקש can teach again.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, he holds it was sanctified for its time
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי ישמעאל, and "it" is ירושלים and the מקדש.

phrases.english: and it was not sanctified for the future to come,
and here we are dealing with a firstborn animal
whose blood was sprinkled before the destruction of the Temple,
and the Temple was destroyed while its meat still exists.
And we compare its meat to its blood,
just as its blood is done on the altar,
so too its meat needs the altar.
phrases.notes: He means the meat may be eaten only while the מזבח is standing.

phrases.english: And he compares tithe to firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15 about רבי ישמעאל's view on קדושה ראשונה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case and giving a separate source (a הקש of meat to blood)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור ruling depends only on whether ירושלים kept its holiness, so it should match מעשר שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בכור ruling is about a בכור whose blood was already sprinkled. Its meat needs a standing מזבח because of the הקש to its blood, and מעשר is compared to בכור.

steps.title: Can something learned from a comparison teach through another comparison?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the בכור rule was itself learned from a הקש. How can it turn around and teach מעשר through another הקש?
steps.simpleTranslation: But can something learned through a הקש go back and teach something else through a הקש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's chain of comparisons: meat to blood, then מעשר to בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a law learned from a הקש cannot itself be the source for another הקש. רבינא's answer uses exactly that kind of double step. So his answer seems to break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A law that was itself learned through a הקש.
Turns around and teaches another law.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the הקש of meat to blood is wrong. It is only asking whether that result can be used again as the base for a second הקש.

phrases.english: But does a matter learned through a comparison
go back and teach through a comparison?
phrases.notes: This is the general rule that in קדשים, a law learned from a הקש can't be used again to teach another הקש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the double הקש in רבינא's answer in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's comparison of מעשר to בכור, when the בכור law was itself learned from a הקש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law learned from a הקש cannot serve as the source for a second הקש. So מעשר cannot be learned from the בכור's meat rule.

steps.title: Grain tithe is non-sacred, so the double comparison is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מעשר דגן is חולין. The ban on a double הקש does not apply here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection in one short line. The rule against a double הקש does not apply, because מעשר דגן counts as חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a law learned from a הקש cannot teach again belongs to קדשים. Here the thing being learned, מעשר דגן, is חולין. So a second הקש onto it is allowed, and רבינא's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe of grain, here meaning מעשר שני of produce.
Non-sacred, not a קרבן or קדשים.

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא: the בכור needs a standing מזבח because its meat is compared to its blood, and מעשר is compared to בכור. A double הקש is allowed here because מעשר דגן is חולין.

phrases.english: Grain tithe is non-sacred.
phrases.notes: The rule against learning from a double הקש is for קדשים, and the thing being learned here is חולין, so the rule doesn't block it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule (the rule applies only to קדשים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule against a double הקש blocks comparing מעשר to the בכור's meat rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר דגן is חולין, so the rule does not apply, and the comparison to בכור works.
